chapter: The McShann band on the road and at the Savoy
title: The Sunday 'Cherokee' broadcast
summary: On their first Sunday matinee Bird and the rhythm section played 'Cherokee' for 45 minutes over the radio and musicians crowded the stand.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: Yeah, I (unintelligible), man, come on, let's have a drink. But --

-- now, that was on a Friday. That Sunday, the first Sunday there at the Savoy, we had to do a matinee which started about 4:00. And so in 15 minutes, we only played two tunes. I think we played something like 'Moten Swing' or something, and then we played 'Cherokee.' And, now, Bird started blowing -- this was up there, as fast as anything Max Roach ever played. I think we were the first band to ever play that extremely fast tempo.
But, anyway, we had it way up there, and --

And somebody from the head office in the studio called that man on the -- that had the earset on, and told him, says, let them go ahead, don't stop them, let them play. And we played 45 minutes more, just the rhythm section and Bird, with the horn setting the riffs from time to time.
On 'Cherokee.' Now, everybody heard this, like, all the guys, the musicians and everybody was -- they
didn't have to go to work until eight that night and they all had tuned in on this thing. And --
Oh, this was on the radio?
And everybody heard it. So that night, you couldn't get close to the bandstand for musicians. Everybody, man, who was that band? You hear that saxophone player? Who was that?
Well, when it came to beating Millender in this battle, I take it that that was really the band, --
